title: A graded surjection induces a closed immersion of relative Proj over a space
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal A=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal A_n$ and $\mathcal B=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal B_n$ be commutative unital graded $\mathcal O_X$-algebras on the small etale site [def-trf-etale-graded-module-algebra] with every component quasi-coherent [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], and let $\varphi:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be a homogeneous algebra homomorphism such that $\varphi_n:\mathcal A_n\to\mathcal B_n$ is surjective for every $n\geq0$. Write $P_X(\mathcal A)$ and $P_X(\mathcal B)$ for the relative Proj spaces with their scheme-test comparisons [lem-sfb-space-relative-proj-scheme-tests], and use tensor pullback [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Then there is a unique morphism $r_\varphi:P_X(\mathcal B)\to P_X(\mathcal A)$ over $X$ with the following property: for every $S$-scheme $W$ and morphism $g:W\to X$, the map $g^*\varphi$ is surjective in every degree, and under the comparisons $W\times_XP_X(\mathcal B)\simeq\operatorname{Proj}_W((g^*\mathcal B)_{\mathrm{Zar}})$ and $W\times_XP_X(\mathcal A)\simeq\operatorname{Proj}_W((g^*\mathcal A)_{\mathrm{Zar}})$ the base change $W\times_Xr_\varphi$ is the morphism of scheme relative Proj induced by the surjection $g^*\varphi$ [prop-nagata-relative-proj-functoriality]. The morphism $r_\varphi$ is a closed immersion of algebraic spaces, meaning that it is representable by schemes [def-trf-algebraic-space] and every scheme base change is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. In particular, for an affine etale chart $u:U=\operatorname{Spec}R\to X$, $U\times_Xr_\varphi$ is the closed immersion $\operatorname{Proj}(\mathcal B(U))\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Proj}(\mathcal A(U))$ induced by the surjective graded ring map $\varphi_U$. The construction is compatible with composition of such surjections and is the identity for $\varphi=\mathrm{id}$. Empty Proj spaces are allowed.

proof.text: For every scheme test $g:W\to X$, tensor pullback is left adjoint to the specified module direct image [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. By [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] it preserves the finite coequalizer expressing each surjection $\varphi_n$ as the cokernel of its kernel. Module sheaves are abelian, with sheafified cokernels [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; hence $g^*\varphi_n$ is surjective. This uses preservation of cokernels, not preservation of kernels or flatness. Its source and target are quasi-coherent by [lem-sfb-space-module-pullback-quasicoherent]. Pass to Zariski modules on $W$ with [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence]; the equivalence and its inverse preserve this cokernel. Denote the resulting graded algebras by $A_g,B_g$ and the map by $\varphi_g$. Products, units and pullback composition are those already supplied with the scheme-test comparisons [lem-sfb-space-relative-proj-scheme-tests]. In successive pullbacks use [def-sfb-space-module-tensor-composition], sending $c\otimes(b\otimes a)$ to $cb'\otimes a$. Naturality of that formula in $a$ identifies the two successive pullbacks of $\varphi$.

source.place: Tag 085F (lemma-morphism-relative-proj), scheme localization; tensor pullback adjunction: sites-modules.tex Tag 03D7 (lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules).

proof.text: First work over a scheme $W$ with a degreewise surjection $\alpha:A\to B$ of quasi-coherent graded algebras. Use [lem-sfb-scheme-proj-veronese-quotient-functor]. On a quasi-compact test $f:T\to W$ send a quotient datum $[d,f,L,\psi]$ for $B$ to $[d,f,L,\psi\circ f^*\alpha^{(d)}]$ for $A$. The degree-one map remains surjective by step 1, applied to schemes, and composition of surjections. If $\beta^{\otimes n}\psi_{an}=\psi'_{a'n}$ witnesses equivalence at a common multiple $ad=a'd'$, precomposing both sides with $f^*\alpha_{adn}$ gives the same witness for the new data. Thus the rule is well-defined. For a scheme map $v:T'\to T$, pulling back this formula gives $v^*\psi\circ v^*f^*\alpha^{(d)}$, which is the formula for $f\circ v$ under the canonical Zariski pullback compositor $v^*f^*\simeq(f\circ v)^*$ of [def-pc-module-pullback], by naturality of that isomorphism in the module. Consequently the rule commutes with test pullback. For non-quasi-compact tests apply it to the compatible family on quasi-compact opens in the cited functor; on a map of arbitrary tests check the same equality on quasi-compact open refinements of inverse images. The representing bijection and [lem-pc-yoneda] give a unique $W$-morphism $c_\alpha:\operatorname{Proj}_W(B)\to\operatorname{Proj}_W(A)$ inducing this operation.

source.place: Tags 01NY (lemma-relative-proj), 01NZ (lemma-glueing-gives-functor-proj), and equation-proj: precomposition on the represented quotient functor.

proof.text: Identify $c_\alpha$ with the ordinary induced Proj map. On an affine base open, write $A(V),B(V)$ for the section graded rings. Quasi-coherent affine chart calculus [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-affine-chart-calculus] makes $\alpha(V)$ surjective in every degree. For homogeneous $b\in B(V)_d$, $d>0$, choose $a\in A(V)_d$ with $\alpha(a)=b$. The opens $D_+(b)$ cover $\operatorname{Proj}(B(V))$ by [prop-nagata-proj-standard-open]. On $D_+(b)$ the normalized quotient in [lem-sfb-scheme-proj-veronese-quotient-functor] is the degree-$d$ twisting quotient. The fraction description of the twist [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf] makes $b$ a basis of $\mathcal O(d)$ there: its inverse sends $x/b^m$ of degree $d$ to $x/b^{m+1}$ of degree zero. Precomposition sends $a$ to this basis. Hence $c_\alpha$ takes this open to $D_+(a)$, with comorphism $x/a^m\mapsto\alpha(x)/b^m$ on degree-zero fractions [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero]. These are precisely the homogeneous localization maps specifying ordinary scheme Proj functoriality. Agreement on this covering proves equality of the morphisms. Clause (3) of [prop-nagata-relative-proj-functoriality] now makes $c_\alpha$ a closed immersion.

source.place: Tag 01NZ, second proof (canonical twisting quotient); lemma-morphism-proj, property (2); Tag 07ZI (lemma-surjective-graded-rings-map-relative-proj).

proof.text: For a scheme map $v:W'\to W$, the scheme-test comparisons of [lem-sfb-space-relative-proj-scheme-tests] identify base change of the two relative Proj schemes with the Proj schemes of $v^*A,v^*B$. On quotient data [lem-sfb-scheme-proj-veronese-quotient-functor], pulling back $\psi\circ f^*\alpha^{(d)}$ is $v'^*\psi\circ v'^*f^*\alpha^{(d)}$ on every further test $v':T'\to T$. The canonical Zariski pullback compositor of [def-pc-module-pullback], natural in the module, identifies the latter with precomposition by the pullback of $\alpha$. Thus the two candidate base-change maps induce the same operation on every quotient class; the representing bijection shows they are equal. This proves compatibility for arbitrary $v$, without a flatness condition, including the identifications between successive scheme tests $W'\to W\to X$. It also proves invariance under the canonical algebra isomorphisms in those comparisons, since inserting an isomorphism and then precomposing is the same composite of graded maps.

source.place: Tags 01NY and 01NZ, functorial quotient description; spaces-divisors.tex Tag 085F, characterization on scheme charts and Tag 085C, base-change comparisons.

proof.text: Construct the space morphism on sections. Put $Q=P_X(\mathcal B)$ and $P=P_X(\mathcal A)$. If $q\in Q(T)$ for an $S$-scheme $T$, let $f=p_Qq\in X(T)$. The pair $(\mathrm{id}_T,q)$ is a section of $T\times_XQ\to T$. By [lem-sfb-space-relative-proj-scheme-tests] it is a section of $\operatorname{Proj}_T(B_f)$. Apply $c_{\varphi_f}$ of steps 2–3 and the inverse comparison for $A_f$; project the resulting section of $T\times_XP$ to obtain $r_T(q)\in P(T)$. Step 4 and compatibility of the comparisons with further scheme base change imply $r_{T'}(q|_{T'})=r_T(q)|_{T'}$ for every $T'\to T$. Thus these functions form a natural transformation, hence a morphism of algebraic spaces by [def-trf-algebraic-space], and it is over $X$ by construction. Applying the same formula to pairs $(t,q)$ over any test $W\to X$ shows its base change is exactly $c_{\varphi_g}$: both send the pair to $(t,r_T(q))$. Conversely any morphism with the required scheme-test property has this same value on $(\mathrm{id}_T,q)$ for each $T,q$. It therefore equals $r$ on every section. This proves existence, uniqueness and the full scheme-test assertion.

source.place: Tag 085F (lemma-morphism-relative-proj), omitted etale-local assembly written sectionwise using the existing scheme-test comparisons.

proof.text: Choose an etale scheme atlas $U\to X$ as in [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Its base change $P\times_XU\to P$ is a surjective etale cover by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], and its source is a scheme by [lem-sfb-space-relative-proj-scheme-tests]. The pullback of $r$ over this cover is $Q\times_XU\to P\times_XU$, which is $c_{\varphi_U}$ and is a closed immersion by step 3. Apply [lem-sfb-space-closed-immersion-atlas-locality], whose hypotheses do not assume representability of $r$: it gives representability and the closed-immersion property on every scheme test of $P$. For an affine etale chart $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\to X$, [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-affine-chart-calculus] computes the cokernel of $\varphi_n$ on sections as zero, so $\varphi_U$ is degreewise surjective. The affine restriction in [prop-nagata-relative-proj-functoriality] identifies this base change with the stated ordinary $\operatorname{Proj}(\mathcal B(U))\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Proj}(\mathcal A(U))$. Here the section graded ring means the direct sum of the component section modules, not sections of an unproved infinite-coproduct identification.

proof.text: For a second degreewise surjection $\beta:\mathcal B\to\mathcal C$, step 2 acts on quotient data by precomposition. Associativity gives $(\psi\circ f^*\beta^{(d)})\circ f^*\varphi^{(d)}=\psi\circ f^*(\beta\circ\varphi)^{(d)}$. Precomposition by the identity fixes every datum. Thus the scheme maps satisfy $c_{\beta\circ\varphi}=c_\varphi\circ c_\beta$ and $c_{\mathrm{id}}=\mathrm{id}$; evaluating the sectionwise construction of step 5 yields the identical equations for $r$. The quotient description is [lem-sfb-scheme-proj-veronese-quotient-functor]. None of these arguments selects a point of a Proj space. If the source Proj is empty, the construction is the unique empty-source map. If the target Proj is empty, step 2 constructs a morphism to the empty scheme on every scheme test, forcing the source test Proj to be empty as well; the sectionwise description then forces $Q$ empty. Consequently all clauses include the empty cases.
